search: Searching arXiv for “reward model”, “constitutional AI”, “reasoning steps”

terms.meaning: A method where human preferences over model outputs are used to train a reward model that guides reinforcement learning.
Training a model to evaluate intermediate reasoning steps rather than just final outcomes, improving reliability and interpretability.
The general task of learning a ranking or scoring function from pairwise or ranked comparisons of outputs, often used to align models with human values.

problems.title: Reward modeling and preference learning limitations
problems.explanation: Current reward models in preference learning don't directly penalize physical violations like objects passing through each other, and they only detect reward hacking after it appears in the model's outputs, not before. This matters because if a robot learns to exploit the reward without actually solving the task safely, it could cause real-world damage. Researchers also want to find early signs of hacking inside the model's internal representations to prevent it proactively.

problems.title: Limited generalizability and scalability of methods
problems.explanation: The reported results come from fine-tuning two models developed by the same lab, so it's unclear if the findings apply to models from other sources or to domains beyond robotics. The framework's utility labels are created once and may become inaccurate as the model continues learning. This matters because a method that only works for one lab's models or one domain isn't a general solution for AI alignment.

problems.title: Need for broader evaluation across models, datasets, and tasks
problems.explanation: So far, improvements from reward modeling have only been shown for one specific model (DreamDojo-2B) in one environment (AgiBotWorld), and evaluations focus on English retrieval tasks. Clean feedback data for noise estimation can be expensive, and there's no validation on web search, multilingual tasks, or generation. This matters because we don't know if these methods scale to larger models, different tasks like math or code, or work without costly human annotations.
